scenarios.metaDescription: Every part of PPM Platform, written as things you can go and check: planned maintenance, work orders, approvals, contracts, VAT invoicing and the rule that keeps each company's data to itself.
scenarios.title: What the platform does, in plain words
scenarios.intro: Every module below is described as behaviour you can go and check for yourself — not a feature list. If you are evaluating the platform, this is what it does. If you are testing it, this is what should happen.
scenarios.footer: Nothing on this page describes how any of it is built. It is the behaviour the product is held to.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.subtitle: Your organisation this morning — what you own, how much of the plan is being kept, and what is on fire.
dashboard.activeAssets: {count, plural, =0 {none in service} one {# in service} other {# in service}}
dashboard.criticalNote: {count, plural, =0 {none critical} one {# critical} other {# critical}}
dashboard.nothingUpcomingBody: Planned visits falling due in the next seven days appear here.
dashboard.alertOverdue: {count, plural, one {# planned visit is overdue} other {# planned visits are overdue}}
dashboard.alertCritical: {count, plural, one {# critical work order is open} other {# critical work orders are open}}

masterData.deleteBody: It stops appearing in lists straight away. Nothing is erased — records that point at it keep working, and an administrator can restore it.
masterData.readOnly: You have read access. Creating and editing is done by an administrator or FM manager.
masterData.resultCount: {total, plural, =0 {No records} one {1 record} other {# records}}

clients.title: Clients
clients.subtitle: The customers whose buildings you maintain. Contracts, invoices and client logins all attach here.
clients.emptyBody: Add the first customer to start attaching sites, contracts and invoices to it.
clients.name: Name
clients.codeHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It appears on contracts and invoices, and is fixed once saved.

locations.title: Locations
locations.subtitle: Every site you maintain. Assets and work orders are dispatched to these.
locations.clientSubtitle: The sites maintained for your account.
locations.emptyBody: Add a site to start attaching assets and work orders to it.
locations.clientEmptyBody: Sites your provider adds for your account will appear here.
locations.name: Name
locations.clientHint: Fixed once saved. A site cannot be moved between clients.

organization.title: Organization
organization.subtitle: Your tenant's profile. It appears on invoices and sets the defaults every module inherits.
organization.name: Organization name
organization.slugHint: Fixed. It keys sign-in links, so it cannot be changed here.
organization.vatNumberHint: 15 digits, as issued by ZATCA. Leave empty if registration is not complete.
organization.missing: This organization could not be loaded.

portal.scopeNote: You see this record and these sites only. Every query the app makes on your behalf is narrowed to your account before it reaches the database.

assets.title: Assets
assets.subtitle: The plant and equipment you maintain. Work orders, PPM schedules and contracts all attach to these.
assets.clientSubtitle: The equipment maintained at your sites.
assets.emptyBody: Add the first piece of equipment to start scheduling maintenance against it.
assets.clientEmptyBody: Equipment your provider registers at your sites will appear here.
assets.name: Name
assets.typeHint: The model or kind within the category — Chiller, AHU, Fire panel.
assets.locationHint: An asset can only move between sites belonging to the same client.
assets.healthHint: Condition from 0 to 100. Set by hand until work-order history can derive it.

technicians.title: Technicians
technicians.subtitle: The people who do the work. Trades and skills here are what dispatch matches a work order against.
technicians.emptyBody: Add the first technician to start assigning preventive and corrective work.
technicians.noMatchesBody: Nobody in the directory matches these filters. Clear them to see everyone.
technicians.name: Name
technicians.skillsPlaceholder: Add a skill, then press Enter
technicians.accountNoneLong: This technician has no sign-in account. They are dispatched through a supervisor.
technicians.accountHint: Only active technician accounts in your organization can be linked, and each account belongs to one technician.
technicians.deleteBody: They stop appearing in the directory and in dispatch straight away. Nothing is erased — completed work orders keep naming them, and an administrator can restore the record.

preventive.title: Preventive maintenance
preventive.subtitle: The planned visits your team works from — what is due, who is doing it, and what has slipped.
preventive.emptyBody: Planned maintenance visits appear here. Schedule one against an asset to start building the calendar.
preventive.dueDateHint: The day the visit is due, not a time.
preventive.deleteBody: The visit is removed from the schedule. Its record is kept for audit.

corrective.title: Corrective maintenance
corrective.subtitle: The faults your team is reacting to — what is broken, how badly, and who has it.
corrective.clientSubtitle: Faults raised at your sites — what you have reported, and where each one has got to.
corrective.emptyBody: Reactive work orders appear here. Raise one against an asset when something fails.
corrective.clientEmptyBody: You have not reported any faults. Raise one against your equipment and the team will pick it up.
corrective.issueHint: What is wrong, in enough detail for whoever picks it up.
corrective.technicianHint: Who is going to do it. Only active technicians are listed.
corrective.unassignToast: Work order returned to the queue.
corrective.deleteBody: The work order is removed from the queue. Its record is kept for audit.

checklists.title: Checklists
checklists.subtitle: The procedures your team works to, and the record of every one carried out.
checklists.runnerOnly: You can run checklists. Writing and editing them is done by a supervisor, administrator or FM manager.
checklists.emptyBody: Write the first procedure to start attaching it to planned visits and work orders.
checklists.name: Name
checklists.categoryHint: The discipline this procedure belongs to. It is how people find it in the library.
checklists.deleteBody: It stops appearing in the library straight away. Nothing is erased — every run it has already produced keeps its own copy of the steps, and an administrator can restore it.
checklists.stepPlaceholder: Add a step, then press Enter
checklists.stepsHint: At least {min}. Drag the handle to reorder, or use the arrows.
checklists.noSteps: No steps yet. Add the first one below.
checklists.requiredOutstanding: {count, plural, one {1 required step left} other {# required steps left}}
checklists.runsSubtitle: Every checklist attached to a job, and how far through it is. This is the evidence an audit reads.
checklists.noRunsBody: Attach a checklist to a planned visit or a work order and it will appear here.
checklists.attachTitle: Attach this checklist to a job
checklists.attachIntro: Choose the job {name} is being carried out for. The steps are copied onto the run, so editing the checklist later will not change what gets recorded here.
checklists.jobHint: Only open jobs are listed. A completed visit or a closed work order cannot take a new checklist.
checklists.noJobs: No open jobs to attach to.

amc.title: AMC & contracts
amc.subtitle: The maintenance contracts you are delivering against — what they are worth, when they end, and how close to spec they are running.
amc.clientSubtitle: The maintenance contracts covering your sites — their term, their value, and how they are performing.
amc.emptyBody: Add the first contract to start tracking its term, its value and its compliance.
amc.clientEmptyBody: Contracts your provider raises for your sites will appear here.
amc.clientHint: Fixed once saved. A contract cannot be moved between clients.
amc.contractNumberHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It appears on invoices, and is fixed once saved.
amc.titleHint: What this contract covers, in the words the client would recognise.
amc.typeHint: What the price includes: parts and labour, labour and consumables, or labour alone.
amc.startDateHint: The first day of the term.
amc.endDateHint: The last day of the term. It must be after the start date.
amc.valueHint: The full term value in riyals, to two decimal places.
amc.complianceHint: How much of the contracted work has been delivered, 0 to 100. Set by hand until PPM history can derive it.
amc.cancelBody: Cancelling is final. The contract stops counting towards your book and towards compliance, and a contract cancelled in error is raised again rather than revived.
amc.deleteBody: The contract is removed from the list. Its record is kept for audit.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.subtitle: Completed work on its way to being billed — who has signed it off, and whose desk it is on now.
approvals.clientSubtitle: Work your provider has completed and is asking you to accept, before it is invoiced.
approvals.clientNote: You are asked to accept work at the client stage.
approvals.approved: Approved — moved to the next stage.
approvals.rejected: Rejected. The chain has stopped here.
approvals.emptyBody: Completed work sent for sign-off will appear here, at the stage it is waiting on.
approvals.rejectBody: The chain stops here and the reason is recorded permanently. Redone work is submitted as a new request.
approvals.reasonHint: What has to change before this can be approved. The requester sees this.
approvals.reasonRequired: Say why this is being rejected.

invoicing.title: Invoicing
invoicing.subtitle: What has been billed, what has been paid, and what is late. Totals and VAT are calculated on the server.
invoicing.clientSubtitle: Your invoices — what is outstanding, what is settled, and the documents themselves.
invoicing.invoiceNumberHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It goes on the bank transfer, and is fixed once saved.
invoicing.workRefHint: The words the client would recognise — the job, the site, the period.
invoicing.amountHint: In riyals, to two decimal places. VAT and the total are calculated on the server.
invoicing.vatNotice: VAT at the rate in force and the total are calculated on the server when this is saved. They cannot be entered here.
invoicing.dueDateHint: Leave empty for the standard 30-day term.
invoicing.notesHint: Payment terms or a reference, printed on the document.
invoicing.withdrawBody: Invoice {number} will be removed from the ledger. A paid invoice cannot be withdrawn.
invoicing.emptyBody: Raise one from an approved job, or directly for a fee or an instalment.
invoicing.clientEmptyBody: Invoices your provider raises will appear here.
invoicing.invoiceCount: {count, plural, =0 {no invoices} one {# invoice} other {# invoices}}
invoicing.sourceHint: An approved job carries its client and description across automatically.
invoicing.approvalHint: Only jobs that have cleared every approval stage and have not been billed appear here.

aiInsights.title: AI insights
aiInsights.subtitle: Four analyses of your own maintenance data, run on the server. Nothing here leaves your organisation's scope.
aiInsights.privacyNote: Each analysis sends a small, capped snapshot of your organisation's own maintenance figures to Anthropic's API from our server. The API key never reaches your browser, no other tenant's data is included, and no client names, user names or money figures are sent.
aiInsights.notConfiguredNote: AI insights are not configured on this deployment.
aiInsights.failed: The analysis could not be run. Try again in a moment.

BREAKDOWN_PATTERNS.title: Repeated breakdowns
BREAKDOWN_PATTERNS.body: The same asset failing twice, or the same fault across a category — and the likely common cause.

PM_OPTIMIZATION.title: Schedule optimisation
PM_OPTIMIZATION.body: Where the preventive plan is visiting too often, and where it is not visiting often enough.

marketing.footerNote: Built for facility maintenance providers in the Gulf.

meta.description: A bilingual maintenance management platform for Gulf facility providers: assets, planned and reactive work, contracts, approvals and VAT invoicing — with every tenant's data isolated by design.

hero.title: Every asset, every visit, every invoice — in one place.
hero.body: PPM Platform runs planned and reactive maintenance for facility providers across the Gulf: the asset register, the PPM calendar, the ticket queue, the approval chain and the VAT invoice that comes out of the end of it.
hero.note: Bilingual English and Arabic. Currency in SAR. VAT at the rate in force.

features.title: What it does
features.body: Eleven modules that cover the work a maintenance provider actually does, from the nameplate on a chiller to the invoice a client pays.

assets.title: Asset register
assets.body: Every piece of plant, where it is, whose it is, and what condition it is in — with photographs attached to the record.

planned.title: Planned maintenance
planned.body: Daily to annual schedules, with compliance measured against what actually fell due rather than against everything ever planned.

approvals.title: Approval chain
approvals.body: Technician, supervisor, FM manager, then the client. Every signature recorded, every stage enforced on the server.

invoicing.title: VAT invoicing
invoicing.body: Invoices raised from approved work, with VAT and totals calculated on the server and a bilingual tax invoice as a PDF.

insights.title: AI insights
insights.body: Failure risk, repeated breakdowns, schedule optimisation and spare-parts forecasting, over your own data and nobody else's.

bilingual.title: English and Arabic
bilingual.body: Not a translation layer — the whole interface mirrors, the typography changes, and every document prints in both languages.

trust.title: Your data is your data
trust.body: Multi-tenancy is not a filter somebody remembered to apply. Every query in this product goes through a data-access layer that injects the organisation — and, for client users, the client — into the filter last, where nothing can displace it.

isolation.title: Isolated by construction
isolation.body: Feature code cannot reach the database directly; a lint rule fails the build if it tries. Cross-tenant reads are tested against a real database, not assumed.

audit.title: Auditable approvals
audit.body: Every approval records who acted, at which stage, in what role, and when. History is appended to and never rewritten.

residency.title: Your own deployment
residency.body: Runs on your infrastructure or ours, against your own MongoDB. Files sit in a private bucket namespaced by tenant and are served only through authenticated routes.

cta.title: See it against your own data
cta.body: Tell us how many sites and assets you run, and we will set up a walkthrough.

pricing.metaDescription: Straightforward monthly pricing for PPM Platform, in Saudi riyals, by the size of the portfolio you maintain.
pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.body: By the size of the portfolio you maintain, in Saudi riyals, per month. Every plan includes both languages, the full module set and unlimited users.
pricing.note: Prices exclude VAT. Annual agreements are discounted. Migration from an existing CMMS is quoted separately and usually takes a fortnight.

enterprise.feature2: AI insights over your own data

contact.title: Talk to us
contact.body: A walkthrough takes half an hour and we will run it against equipment you recognise. Tell us how many sites you maintain and we will come prepared.
